title: PNG decoding as the original's decodeImage sees it in Chrome
scope: PNG bytes to the RGBA that createImageBitmap (colorSpaceConversion none, premultiplyAlpha none), canvas drawImage and getImageData give in Chrome, including which damaged files are left out, APNG frame 0 and the canvas premultiply round trip.
acceptance: Every RGBA byte, dimension and omission equals actual Chrome on fixed named probes, truncation and flip sweeps and CRC-fixed structural mutations, with host limits counted separately.
Own pure-Rust code with no dependency; a deliberately wrong pixel is rejected.

evidence.summary: 5,532 committed cases (named, sweep, structural) and the 13 audit PNG fixtures equal Chrome 156 byte for byte offline; live fresh-seed runs and about 70,000 development cases with zero divergences outside the host-limit class; sabotage rejected. No acceptance claim.

open_items: Not wired into readCompanions/scanCompanions: the decoder exists, the ordered companion continuation (MTL text, name order, omission) is still io.obj.companions.images.
Chrome only, one version (156.0.8078.79) on Linux. No Wasm runtime comparison and no other browser.
Inferred, not observed: a very large IDAT chunk may reach Chrome's decoder in pieces; the post-image rules assume the whole chunk is fed at once.
Host-limit class: images over PngLimits (default 2^26 pixels, 256 MiB input) are refused where Chrome may decode or fail differently.
Not in ci/native-suites.json and not wired to cargo xtask fuzz (rust/xtask is held by one PR at a time).
Release decode is about 155 ms for a 2048 by 2048 RGBA image; not tuned.
